methods.source_pins: Independently recomputed all 16 files enumerated in evidence.json; every digest and byte count matched.
methods.invented_tests: Copied frozen packet to a fresh /tmp directory and ran its bounded test_tiny.py with 30s timeout, nice 15 and one-thread BLAS/Numba environment; output was {"status":"passed","tests":40}. No actual graph was imported or evaluated.
methods.independent_counterexamples: Ran reproduce.py on a separate temporary copy. Full selected record identity rejects a changed exposure. The completed() helper accepted a self-authored success-shaped controller marker when passed its computed raw digest, despite no retained tool-return acknowledgment and an empty comparison_artifacts map.

passed_findings: Single selected integer ordinal 2–7 and one phase are bound through selection, resource receipt, worker authorization and result rows; fixed masses remain 0.125 and population_cut_v1 target identity checks bind complete record, problem, composition, parent ID and upstream identity.

Dynamic-witness stage explicitly rebuilds first-parent dynamic graph, evaluates selected whole parent at exact three saved points, validates those outputs against that parent's saved dynamic calls, and produces newly owned plus/minus finite-difference calls. This closes the predecessor's missing derivative witness for ordinals 2–7; it does not reuse parent1's derivatives.

Fixed-selected stage independently builds the selected native parent graph, requires the selected witness acknowledgment, compares exact common points, all factor arrays, poll/logp, rates, physical outputs and declared finite differences. It does not normalize conditionals or infer other parents.

Complete 662-coordinate points and digests, source/contract pins, exact parent exposure/source record, FD variable/coordinate/step/point arithmetic and ordered call rosters are checked in the comparison path. Mutating the complete exposure changed the parent identity and failed validation in my isolated test.

Normal process failure leaves an exclusive attempt that refuses a new run; completed replay is read-only. Controller tears down and reaps its owned process group on handled exception/interruption; tiny tests exercise receipt-write and interruption failures. Runtime hard limits and sampled watchdogs are explicit, but remain unmeasured on an actual graph.

material_gap.location: selection.py: completed(); launch.py: fixed-selected witness precondition
material_gap.reproduction: reproduce.py creates only result.json, terminal.json and a self-authored controller-success.json with correct-looking fields and empty comparison_artifacts. It computes sha256 locally and calls completed(out, digest, 2, 'dynamic-witness'). The helper accepts it. No retained write_stdin_return object, stdout acknowledgment or caller-return pin is presented.
material_gap.effect: For fixed-selected, launch.py uses completed() as the pre-launch witness gate. Thus a success-shaped but unacknowledged/incomplete marker with the supplied digest can satisfy the helper and let the expensive fixed graph launch before the later comparison gate reruns compare_witness. The later gate should prevent a false final comparison receipt, but it is too late to enforce the claimed pre-launch acknowledgment requirement.
material_gap.comparison_artifact_specific: completed() iterates whatever comparison_artifacts entries the receipt contains but never requires the exact phase-specific set. Empty mapping passes. Actual frozen workflow writes named execution and phase-comparison artifacts, so requiring those exact schemas and pins would reject the reproduced marker.
material_gap.boundary: This is a local workflow/protocol validation gap, not proof against malicious same-user filesystem/code control. A raw SHA proves only bytes. The frozen V1 prose says the caller must retain successful tool output, but this new-stage precondition does not accept or verify that retained return; unlike predecessor authentication, the requirement is currently out of band.

required_successor_checks: Bind an externally retained successful caller-return JSON (or an equivalent independently reviewed acknowledgment object) to phase, selected ordinal, exact controller-success digest and expected controller stdout; require it before fixed-selected can reserve/launch.
Require an exact comparison_artifacts roster and validate the expected artifact paths/schemas for each phase; reject empty, missing, extra or parent-aliased entries.
Add tiny negative cases for self-authored marker + raw digest, empty/missing comparison artifact map and mismatched caller-return contents; retain the existing predecessor acknowledgment tests.
limitations: No actual graph, compiler, model, fit or forecast ran; no actual resource feasibility or real-stage cleanup is demonstrated.
The 40 tiny tests use invented/synthetic receipt and numerical fixtures; they test orchestration, not scientific numerical truth.
Even a corrected retained-return gate is cooperating local workflow provenance, not cryptographic same-user attestation or protection from arbitrary coherent source/filesystem rewriting.
Pointwise equality and FD witnesses do not establish conditional normalizers, sampler convergence, posterior validity, all-parent inference or predictive qualification.
